read.thesis: Record $220.3B backlog (doubled y/y) on $71.6B Marine orders; supply-side signal is Electric Boat throughput up 30% and shipbuilders rising to 8,000, with FY26 EPS guide raised to $17.20–17.30 and capex 3.5–4% of sales.

utilisation.quote: we're up 30% this year versus the same time last year

capex.quote: we continue to expect capital expenditures between 3.5% and 4% of sales for the full year

triggers.label: FY26 EPS raised to $17.20–17.30

triggers.label: Backlog $220.3B, up 100.6% y/y

triggers.label: Marine margin lifted by one-time catch-up
triggers.quote: we actually had a onetime cumulative catch pickup on the booking rate, which spiked the margin a little bit in the quarter

guidance.quote: we once again increased our forecast to between $17.20 to $17.30 per diluted share
This contemplates revenue between $56.5 billion to $56.8 billion and operating margin around 10.5%
we continue to expect capital expenditures between 3.5% and 4% of sales for the full year
We continue to expect free cash flow conversion at around 105% for the year
our expectation for net interest expense for the year is approximately $215 million
think about the Marine Group being in that mid-7% range as a baseline

we expect the G300 to be certified towards the end of next year
We continue to be hyper-focused on delivering the first Columbia and first Virginia VPM ships by the end of 2028
